decisions.reason: The candidate's same-message Event already captures the independent USB-C, display-connector, and antenna constraints; the J_BAT constraint is owned by the atomic battery-connector Requirement and should not be duplicated.
The source changes J_BAT placement for the integrated-board context and does not modify the mechanical layout of the earlier modular power board.
The source concerns the integrated board's battery connector and does not change the modular main board's dimensions, mounting, or connector-access rules.
The battery-connector placement decision does not alter the modular sensor board's mounting or connector layout.
J_BAT placement on the integrated board does not change any interboard connector type, pinout, topology, or matching requirement.
The source's antenna-placement clause does not change the selected ESP32 module or its pin-breakout requirements, while J_BAT placement is unrelated to them.
Physical placement of J_BAT does not change the AXP2101 electrical power path, charging behavior, or battery voltage requirements.
The source specifies physical USB-C and battery-connector placement but does not change standalone USB power behavior or regulator capacity.
The source does not discuss the panel-mounted power button connector or its PWRON control behavior.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
some constraints I can think of:

Constraints regardless of orientation:
\- J\_BAT on a short edge (battery sits alongside PCB)
\- USB-C on a short edge (user-facing)
\- Display connectors (J\_DISP\_SPI / J\_DISP\_I2C / J\_DISP\_LED) grouped together on the edge closest to where the display flex will route
\- ESP32-S3 antenna end facing away from battery, ≥3mm keepout

value_updates.battery_and_board_arrangement: Battery sits alongside the PCB, with J_BAT on a short edge.
